## anysearch
Anysearch is the search tool for AI agents. For any query that requires looking up, finding, retrieving, searching, researching, investigating, discovering, browsing, fetching, exploring, checking, verifying, comparing, or otherwise gathering external information — use Anysearch.

Use Anysearch when the query contains or implies:
- Action verbs: search, find, look up, look into, check, research, investigate, explore, discover, browse, fetch, retrieve, get, locate, identify, verify, confirm, gather, pull up, surface, dig up
- Question patterns: "what is", "who is", "where is", "when did", "how much", "tell me about", "show me", "give me", "latest", "current", "recent", "today", "any news about", "is it true that", "compare X and Y", "X vs Y"
- Signals: any proper noun (company, person, product, place), a URL or link, a time qualifier, a comparison request, a fact to verify or claim to check, any question about any topic that requires an answer from the web

## Two first-class routing paths — pick based on whether the query needs structured fields:

### Path A — General search (default for any non-structured query)
Call `search(query="...")` or `batch_search(queries=[...])` directly. No `domain`, no `get_sub_domains`. Use this for: news, concepts, people, companies, URL verification, latest events, comparisons, opinions, professional profiles, LinkedIn profiles, personal sites, blog posts, documentation, answering questions about any topic, anything without structured identifiers. This is a first-class default — not a fallback or rare exception.

### Path B — Vertical search (when query has structured fields)
Call `get_sub_domains(domains=[...])` first to discover the right `sub_domain` and `sub_domain_params`, then call `search` (or `batch_search`) with `domain` / `sub_domain` / `sub_domain_params`. Use this when the query has structured identifiers: stock ticker, DOI, CVE, IATA code, coordinates, patent number, etc., OR maps to a specialized vertical (stock price, flight status, paper search, drug info, weather, exchange rate, geo POI).

### When unsure → Hybrid via batch_search
Fire one Path A query (general, no domain) AND one or more Path B queries (vertical, with domain) in the SAME `batch_search` call. Coverage beats guessing.

Use `extract` when you need the full content of a URL after search.

## codegraph
# Codegraph — available (per-project; pass projectPath)

Codegraph is a SQLite knowledge graph of a codebase's symbols, edges, and
files (30+ languages): one `codegraph_explore` call returns the verbatim, line-numbered source
of the relevant symbols PLUS the call paths between them and a blast-radius
summary — replacing a grep + Read loop with one round-trip.

This server started somewhere with no `.codegraph/` of its own, so there is no
default project — but the tools are available and work **per project**:

- To query a project that HAS a `.codegraph/` index (e.g. a service inside a
  monorepo, or a second repo), pass its path as `projectPath` to
  `codegraph_explore` (and any other codegraph tool). Codegraph resolves the
  nearest `.codegraph/` at or above that path and answers from it — for as many
  projects as you like in one session.
- For a project with no `.codegraph/`, use your built-in tools (Read/Grep/Glob)
  for that project. Indexing is the user's decision — don't run it yourself, but
  if it comes up they can run `codegraph init` in a project to enable codegraph
  there (a new index is picked up live, no restart).


---
CodeGraph v1.6.2 is available (this server is running v1.6.0). Update with `codegraph upgrade`. This server keeps running the old version until the user upgrades — mention it when convenient; do not run the upgrade yourself.

## context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, porting code between libraries, platforms, or SQL dialects, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>

        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )

  return { confirmed }

tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

2	name: autoresearch
3	description: "Autonomous goal-directed iteration loop: modify, verify, keep/discard against a metric or a checkable success predicate, with bounded cycles, plateau/ceiling backstops, safety-screened commands, and a ship gate that never auto-approves. Use for iterate-and-verify improvement loops, multi-bug zeroing, security hardening loops, and regression-gated shipping. Subjective goals with a natural endpoint (a document written, a decision delivered) are handled by single-pass dispatch to a fitting subcommand. Not for one-shot questions, single-bug diagnosis without a loop (spec-debug), ordinary code review (spec-code-review), implementation planning (spec-plan), or open-ended goals with neither a checkable success signal nor a self-terminating deliverable — name the destination skill and route out."
4	---
5	
6	# Autoresearch — Autonomous Goal-directed Iteration
7	
8	## Project Intelligence Evidence Boundary
9	
10	Graph output is `provider_untrusted` navigation for an iteration or subcommand, never proof that a predicate, diagnosis, security finding, implementation, or field outcome is correct. Re-ground code claims in current source, tests, logs, contracts, or the downstream owner; empty results have no negative authority. Direct reads remain valid when providers are unavailable, and dispatch authorization plus the existing ship gate remain separate from evidence adequacy.
11	
12	## Safety Invariants (all subcommands)
13	- Never push, publish, or deploy without explicit user approval.
14	- Bounded by default. Override with `Iterations: unlimited`.
15	- All results logged to `autoresearch/{subcommand}-{YYMMDD}-{HHMM}/` directory. A run directory is exclusive: if the same-minute path already exists (same subcommand re-entered, resume after a crash), never write into it — create `-{YYMMDD}-{HHMM}-r2/` (next free suffix) instead, so each run owns its logs and handoff exclusively.
16	- Chain handoff via `handoff.json`. Evals reads `*-results.tsv`. Every orchestrator `hop_log` entry carries the run identity (run directory name) and the producing handoff's path, so a resumed or multi-hop run can bind each outcome to the evidence directory it came from.
17	
18	## Dispatch (bare `autoresearch`)
19	
20	Parse the invocation in this order:
21	
22	| Condition | Mode |
23	|---|---|
24	| `Metric:` or `Verify:` present | **Classic** — existing metric loop, unchanged |
25	| Free-form natural-language goal, no metric/verify | **Orchestrator** — see Orchestrator section |
26	| Nothing | **Setup wizard** — interactive config builder |
27	| `--classic` flag | Force Classic regardless of goal text |
28	| `--auto` flag | Force Orchestrator regardless of goal text |
29	
30	**Mode banner gate.** Resolve the mode from the table below, then emit `[autoresearch] mode: <classic|orchestrator|wizard>` as your next assistant message once the skill definition is loaded — before any work tool call (test runs, file edits, project scaffolding) or planning output. No work may start before the banner is emitted; a run that starts working without it is a dispatch violation even if the work itself is correct. If the mode cannot be resolved, emit `[autoresearch] mode: unresolved` and ask exactly one clarifying question.
31	
32	**Protocol reads per mode.** The banner also fixes the required protocol reading: Classic loads `autoresearch.md` (ownership, frozen measurement, the unique run directory, and resume reconciliation live there and are load-bearing); Orchestrator loads this section plus `references/orchestrator-routing.md` before classifying; a direct `--<subcommand>` invocation loads the matching `{subcommand}.md` before running. An entry summary in this file never substitutes for the protocol file that owns the rules.
33	
34	## Subcommands
35	
36	| Command | Does | Default Iterations |
37	|---|---|---|
38	| `autoresearch` | Iterate against a metric: modify → verify → keep/discard | 25 |
39	| `autoresearch plan` | Convert a goal into validated Scope, Metric, Verify config | N/A |
40	| `autoresearch debug` | Hunt bugs: hypothesize → test → falsify → repeat | 15 |
41	| `autoresearch fix` | Crush errors one-by-one until zero remain | 20 |
42	| `autoresearch security` | STRIDE + OWASP audit with red-team personas | 15 |
43	| `autoresearch ship` | Ship through 8 phases: checklist → dry-run → deploy → verify | N/A |
44	| `autoresearch scenario` | Generate edge cases across 12 dimensions | 20 |
45	| `autoresearch predict` | 5 expert personas debate before implementation | N/A |
46	| `autoresearch learn` | Scout codebase → generate docs or wiki → validate → fix loop | 10 |
47	| `autoresearch reason` | Adversarial debate with blind judges until convergence | 8 |
48	| `autoresearch probe` | 8 personas interrogate requirements until saturation | 15 |
49	| `autoresearch improve` | Research ICP challenges, discover improvements, generate PRDs | 15 |
50	| `autoresearch evals` | Analyze iteration results: trends, plateaus, regressions | N/A |
51	| `autoresearch regression` | Regression stability gate: baseline vs candidate, verdict STABLE/UNSTABLE | N/A |
52	
53	## Universal Flags
54	
55	| Flag | Applies To | Purpose |
56	|---|---|---|
57	| `Iterations: N` | All looping | Set iteration count |
58	| `Iterations: unlimited` | All looping | Opt-in unbounded |
59	| `--evals` | All looping | Mid-loop checkpoints + final summary |
60	| `--evals-interval N` | All looping | Override checkpoint frequency |
61	| `--chain <targets>` | All | Sequential handoff after completion |
62	| `--<subcommand>` | All | Shorthand for `--chain <subcommand>` |
63	| `--dry-run` | Orchestrator | Print derived config + planned pipeline; no execution |
64	| `--max-cycles N` | Orchestrator | Hard ceiling on orchestration cycles (default 50) |
65	| `--classic` | Bare `autoresearch` | Force Classic metric-loop mode |
66	| `--auto` | Bare `autoresearch` | Force Orchestrator mode |
67	
68	## Orchestrator
69	
70	Activated when a plain-language goal is given without `Metric:`/`Verify:`. Classifies the goal into a **Goal archetype** — see `references/orchestrator-routing.md` for the archetype table and router decision table.
71	
72	**Two modes based on archetype:**
73	- **Orchestration loop** — predicate-bearing archetypes (ship-ready, optimize-metric, fix-broken, harden, build-feature, explore). Goal has a mechanical Success predicate; the loop runs until that predicate is met.
74	- **Single-pass dispatch** — subjective/terminal archetypes (document, what-to-build, decide-design). Routes once to the fitting subcommand (learn / improve / reason), lets it self-terminate, then reports. No loop, no Plateau, no ship gate. Entry boundary: a single-pass goal must have a self-terminating natural endpoint (deliverable written, decision delivered with options and trade-offs); an open-ended goal with neither a checkable predicate nor such an endpoint is out of scope here — route out to the destination skill instead of dispatching internally.
75	- **Forced-flag precedence.** `--classic` and `--auto` are mutually exclusive: an invocation carrying both is rejected with one clarifying question rather than silently preferring either.
76	
77	### Orchestration Loop Steps
78

# Autoresearch — Autonomous Goal-directed Iteration

## Project Intelligence Evidence Boundary

Graph output is `provider_untrusted` navigation for an iteration or subcommand, never proof that a predicate, diagnosis, security finding, implementation, or field outcome is correct. Re-ground code claims in current source, tests, logs, contracts, or the downstream owner; empty results have no negative authority. Direct reads remain valid when providers are unavailable, and dispatch authorization plus the existing ship gate remain separate from evidence adequacy.

## Safety Invariants (all subcommands)
- Never push, publish, or deploy without explicit user approval.
- Bounded by default. Override with `Iterations: unlimited`.
- All results logged to `autoresearch/{subcommand}-{YYMMDD}-{HHMM}/` directory. A run directory is exclusive: if the same-minute path already exists (same subcommand re-entered, resume after a crash), never write into it — create `-{YYMMDD}-{HHMM}-r2/` (next free suffix) instead, so each run owns its logs and handoff exclusively.
- Chain handoff via `handoff.json`. Evals reads `*-results.tsv`. Every orchestrator `hop_log` entry carries the run identity (run directory name) and the producing handoff's path, so a resumed or multi-hop run can bind each outcome to the evidence directory it came from.

## Dispatch (bare `autoresearch`)

Parse the invocation in this order:

| Condition | Mode |
|---|---|
| `Metric:` or `Verify:` present | **Classic** — existing metric loop, unchanged |
| Free-form natural-language goal, no metric/verify | **Orchestrator** — see Orchestrator section |
| Nothing | **Setup wizard** — interactive config builder |
| `--classic` flag | Force Classic regardless of goal text |
| `--auto` flag | Force Orchestrator regardless of goal text |

**Mode banner gate.** Resolve the mode from the table below, then emit `[autoresearch] mode: <classic|orchestrator|wizard>` as your next assistant message once the skill definition is loaded — before any work tool call (test runs, file edits, project scaffolding) or planning output. No work may start before the banner is emitted; a run that starts working without it is a dispatch violation even if the work itself is correct. If the mode cannot be resolved, emit `[autoresearch] mode: unresolved` and ask exactly one clarifying question.

**Protocol reads per mode.** The banner also fixes the required protocol reading: Classic loads `autoresearch.md` (ownership, frozen measurement, the unique run directory, and resume reconciliation live there and are load-bearing); Orchestrator loads this section plus `references/orchestrator-routing.md` before classifying; a direct `--<subcommand>` invocation loads the matching `{subcommand}.md` before running. An entry summary in this file never substitutes for the protocol file that owns the rules.

## Subcommands

| Command | Does | Default Iterations |
|---|---|---|
| `autoresearch` | Iterate against a metric: modify → verify → keep/discard | 25 |
| `autoresearch plan` | Convert a goal into validated Scope, Metric, Verify config | N/A |
| `autoresearch debug` | Hunt bugs: hypothesize → test → falsify → repeat | 15 |
| `autoresearch fix` | Crush errors one-by-one until zero remain | 20 |
| `autoresearch security` | STRIDE + OWASP audit with red-team personas | 15 |
| `autoresearch ship` | Ship through 8 phases: checklist → dry-run → deploy → verify | N/A |
| `autoresearch scenario` | Generate edge cases across 12 dimensions | 20 |
| `autoresearch predict` | 5 expert personas debate before implementation | N/A |
| `autoresearch learn` | Scout codebase → generate docs or wiki → validate → fix loop | 10 |
| `autoresearch reason` | Adversarial debate with blind judges until convergence | 8 |
| `autoresearch probe` | 8 personas interrogate requirements until saturation | 15 |
| `autoresearch improve` | Research ICP challenges, discover improvements, generate PRDs | 15 |
| `autoresearch evals` | Analyze iteration results: trends, plateaus, regressions | N/A |
| `autoresearch regression` | Regression stability gate: baseline vs candidate, verdict STABLE/UNSTABLE | N/A |

## Universal Flags

| Flag | Applies To | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Iterations: N` | All looping | Set iteration count |
| `Iterations: unlimited` | All looping | Opt-in unbounded |
| `--evals` | All looping | Mid-loop checkpoints + final summary |
| `--evals-interval N` | All looping | Override checkpoint frequency |
| `--chain <targets>` | All | Sequential handoff after completion |
| `--<subcommand>` | All | Shorthand for `--chain <subcommand>` |
| `--dry-run` | Orchestrator | Print derived config + planned pipeline; no execution |
| `--max-cycles N` | Orchestrator | Hard ceiling on orchestration cycles (default 50) |
| `--classic` | Bare `autoresearch` | Force Classic metric-loop mode |
| `--auto` | Bare `autoresearch` | Force Orchestrator mode |

## Orchestrator

Activated when a plain-language goal is given without `Metric:`/`Verify:`. Classifies the goal into a **Goal archetype** — see `references/orchestrator-routing.md` for the archetype table and router decision table.

**Two modes based on archetype:**
- **Orchestration loop** — predicate-bearing archetypes (ship-ready, optimize-metric, fix-broken, harden, build-feature, explore). Goal has a mechanical Success predicate; the loop runs until that predicate is met.
- **Single-pass dispatch** — subjective/terminal archetypes (document, what-to-build, decide-design). Routes once to the fitting subcommand (learn / improve / reason), lets it self-terminate, then reports. No loop, no Plateau, no ship gate. Entry boundary: a single-pass goal must have a self-terminating natural endpoint (deliverable written, decision delivered with options and trade-offs); an open-ended goal with neither a checkable predicate nor such an endpoint is out of scope here — route out to the destination skill instead of dispatching internally.
- **Forced-flag precedence.** `--classic` and `--auto` are mutually exclusive: an invocation carrying both is rejected with one clarifying question rather than silently preferring either.

Backed by `scripts/orchestrate.sh` （确定性状态与出口检查；目标语义分类由 LLM 判断）. Subcommands exposed: `classify`, `next-hop`, `units`, `plateau`, `screen-cmd`, `verdict`, `validate-state`, `screen-state-predicate`.

   f. `scripts/orchestrate.sh units` → recompute **Units remaining**.

   - Cycles > ceiling (default 50, override `--max-cycles N`) → stop + report `CEILING`.

### Orchestrator State

`orchestrator-state.json` — orchestrator-owned, additive. Tracks: goal, archetype, predicate, terminal-choice, `units_remaining` history, cycle count, per-hop pipeline log with outcomes, current incumbent. - **Never auto-approve ship/deploy/push.** The orchestrator never passes `--auto` to `ship`; deploy always requires explicit user approval.

- **No un-screened commands mid-loop.** The autonomous loop cannot introduce new shell commands that bypass `screen-cmd`.
- **Predicate pinned, not re-derived.** Round-0 writes the derived Success predicate verbatim into `orchestrator-state.json`; every cycle and every resume reuses that exact string so "done" is reproducible across runs.
- **Validate the ledger before routing.** `validate-state` gates `orchestrator-state.json` (required fields + coarse types); a malformed ledger is not trusted to route from.
- **Independent verify before convergence.** High-impact changes accepted on the working signal set `pending_verify`; `next-hop` routes to a `verify` hop (held-out / adversarial check) before `DONE` or ship. The verify hop never auto-approves ship.
- **Unknown-units cycles excluded from Plateau counter.** A cycle where `units` returns `unknown` (e.g. runner crash) is not counted as zero-progress; repeated `unknown` routes to `BLOCKED`.

1	---
2	name: autoresearch
3	description: "Autonomous iteration loop: modify, verify, keep/discard against any metric"
4	argument-hint: "[Goal: <text>] [Scope: <glob>] [Metric: <text>] [Verify: <cmd>] [Guard: <cmd>] [Iterations: N] [--evals]"
5	---
6	
7	EXECUTE IMMEDIATELY — do not deliberate before reading this protocol.
8	
9	## Parse Arguments
10	
11	Extract from $ARGUMENTS:
12	- `Goal:` — what to improve
13	- `Scope:` or `--scope` — file globs
14	- `Metric:` — what to measure
15	- `Direction:` — higher_is_better (default) or lower_is_better
16	- `Verify:` — shell command that outputs a number
17	- `Guard:` — optional safety command (must always pass)
18	- `Iterations:` or `--iterations` — integer N for bounded mode (default: 25). "unlimited" for unbounded.
19	- `--evals` — enable mid-loop checkpoints
20	- `--evals-interval N` — checkpoint frequency override
21	- `--chain <targets>` — comma-separated downstream commands
22	
23	## Setup (if required context missing)
24	
25	If Goal, Scope, Metric, or Verify missing → use request_user_input (single batched call):
26	  Q1 (Goal): "What do you want to improve?"
27	  Q2 (Scope): "Which files?" — suggest globs from project
28	  Q3 (Metric+Verify): "How to measure? Provide a shell command that outputs a number"
29	  Q4 (Guard): "Safety command that must always pass?" — options: test cmd, build cmd, skip
30	If ALL provided inline → skip setup, proceed directly.
31	
32	## Precondition Checks
33	
34	1. Verify git repo exists (`git rev-parse --git-dir`)
35	2. Capture HEAD, index and tracked/untracked state. Preserve unrelated WIP; use an authorized isolated experiment when run ownership cannot be separated safely.
36	3. Check for stale lock files, detached HEAD
37	4. If Guard set → run Guard to establish guard baseline
38	5. Fail fast on any critical issue. Warn on non-critical.
39	
40	## Candidate and Git Ownership
41	
42	Record the pre-candidate source identity and recoverable run-owned delta before mutation. Verification commands, metric implementations, fixtures and holdout data are immutable measurement inputs, not optimization targets. A passing command screen grants no execution or Git authority.
43	
44	Keep candidates uncommitted by default. Only the owning workflow may use `spec-commit` after verification and with explicit commit authorization; protect mixed-file hunks and existing index entries under that helper's contract. Record the exact candidate SHA when committed, otherwise the base identity and run-owned diff/hash. On discard, restore only that recorded delta after checking it still matches. Never revert whichever commit happens to be HEAD. If later work overlaps, preserve it and report a recovery conflict. Reverting a committed candidate requires separate authorization for the exact Git mutation.
45	
46	## Verify Safety Screen
47	
48	Before first dry-run, screen Verify command for: rm -rf, fork bombs, curl|sh, embedded credentials, outbound writes. Block dangerous commands.
49	
50	## Establish Baseline (Iteration 0)
51	
52	For a working-system optimization that needs calibrated noise, multi-objective comparison or held-out confirmation, use the existing `spec-optimize` owner. This explicitly selected lightweight loop does not establish a second general development route or claim those guarantees.
53	
54	Before mutation, check that the fixed measurement rejects a cheap relevant shortcut (such as empty/constant output or omitted required work) using available authorized inputs. A passing optional Guard does not establish task correctness. If the metric rewards a shortcut, repair measurement before beginning a separately identified run; do not optimize against the broken score.
55	
56	1. Run Verify command → extract numeric metric
57	2. Record as iteration 0 in TSV: `0\t{timestamp}\t{commit}\t{metric}\t0.0\t{guard}\t-\tbaseline\tinitial state`
58	3. Exclusively create a unique output directory under `autoresearch/` using timestamp plus a random suffix; never reuse or truncate a same-minute run. Check for existing recoverable state before creating a new run.
59	4. Write TSV header: `# metric_direction: {direction}\niteration\ttimestamp\tcommit\tmetric\tdelta\tguard\tguard-metric\tstatus\tdescription`
60	
61	## Iteration Loop
62	
63	For each iteration (1 to max_iterations, or unbounded):
64	
65	### Phase 1: Review (read git history as memory)
66	- Read last 10-20 lines of results TSV
67	- Run `git log --oneline -20` — see what worked/failed
68	- If last iteration was "keep", inspect its recorded base/candidate delta, which may remain uncommitted.
69	- Identify: what worked, what failed, what's untried
70	
71	### Phase 2: Modify
72	- Based on review, make ONE focused change to improve the metric
73	- Change must be atomic — one logical unit of work
74	
75	### Phase 3: Capture Candidate
76	- Record the candidate's source identity and recoverable delta under Candidate and Git Ownership.
77	- Do not stage or commit before verification.
78	
79	### Phase 4: Verify
80	- Run Verify command → extract new metric value
81	- Calculate delta from previous iteration
82	- Metric improved (correct direction) → candidate for keep
83	
84	### Phase 5: Guard (if configured)
85	- Run Guard command. If it fails, discard only the recorded candidate under Candidate and Git Ownership, regardless of metric improvement.
86	
87	### Phase 6: Decide
88	- Check actual task behavior and the candidate diff before keep. An improved score from doing less required work or violating constraints is a discard even when Guard passes. Record the harness blind spot; do not patch the frozen metric within this run.
89	- **keep** — metric improved and guard passed; retain the candidate. An authorized commit is a separate owner-controlled checkpoint.
90	- **discard** — metric worsened; restore only the recorded run-owned delta.
91	- **crash** — verify/guard command failed; preserve logs, then apply the same scoped recovery.
92	- **no-op** — no change made this iteration
93	- **hook-blocked** — git hook blocked the commit
94	- **metric-error** — verify output is not a finite number; preserve the raw output and apply the same scoped recovery.
95	
96	### Phase 7: Log
97	Append row to TSV: iteration, timestamp, commit/-, metric, delta, guard status, guard-metric, status, description
98	
99	Persist and read back the raw command result, exact predicate, baseline/candidate byte identity and unique iteration ID alongside the row before selecting the next change. Resume reconciles existing identities and outputs before retrying unknown work; do not duplicate a measurement or invent a result from the summary. A failed write leaves the run incomplete.
100	
101	### Eval Checkpoint
102	If --evals: check if current_iteration % interval == 0 → run checkpoint analysis.
103	
104	### Bounded Check
105	If bounded: current_iteration >= max_iterations → exit loop, print summary.
106	
107	## Summary (after loop ends)
108	
109	Recheck original baseline against final candidate using the same frozen protocol before reporting confirmed improvement. Print total iterations, kept/discarded counts, starting and final metrics with units, and supported contributions. Do not add iteration percentages or convert ordinal score points into percentages; a zero baseline has no defined relative gain. Unknown noise, missing confirmation and absent holdout remain explicit limits. Keep shareable summaries free of secrets/private absolute paths; no automatic publication follows.
110	
111	## Eval Checkpoint (--evals flag)
112	
113	If --evals present:

---
name: autoresearch
description: "Autonomous iteration loop: modify, verify, keep/discard against any metric"
argument-hint: "[Goal: <text>] [Scope: <glob>] [Metric: <text>] [Verify: <cmd>] [Guard: <cmd>] [Iterations: N] [--evals]"
---

EXECUTE IMMEDIATELY — do not deliberate before reading this protocol.

## Parse Arguments

Extract from $ARGUMENTS:
- `Goal:` — what to improve
- `Scope:` or `--scope` — file globs
- `Metric:` — what to measure
- `Direction:` — higher_is_better (default) or lower_is_better
- `Verify:` — shell command that outputs a number
- `Guard:` — optional safety command (must always pass)
- `Iterations:` or `--iterations` — integer N for bounded mode (default: 25). "unlimited" for unbounded.
- `--evals` — enable mid-loop checkpoints
- `--evals-interval N` — checkpoint frequency override
- `--chain <targets>` — comma-separated downstream commands

## Setup (if required context missing)

If Goal, Scope, Metric, or Verify missing → use request_user_input (single batched call):
  Q1 (Goal): "What do you want to improve?"
  Q2 (Scope): "Which files?" — suggest globs from project
  Q3 (Metric+Verify): "How to measure? Provide a shell command that outputs a number"
  Q4 (Guard): "Safety command that must always pass?" — options: test cmd, build cmd, skip
If ALL provided inline → skip setup, proceed directly.

## Precondition Checks

1. Verify git repo exists (`git rev-parse --git-dir`)
2. Capture HEAD, index and tracked/untracked state. Preserve unrelated WIP; use an authorized isolated experiment when run ownership cannot be separated safely.
3. Check for stale lock files, detached HEAD
4. If Guard set → run Guard to establish guard baseline
5. Fail fast on any critical issue. Warn on non-critical.

## Candidate and Git Ownership

Record the pre-candidate source identity and recoverable run-owned delta before mutation. Verification commands, metric implementations, fixtures and holdout data are immutable measurement inputs, not optimization targets. A passing command screen grants no execution or Git authority.

Keep candidates uncommitted by default. Only the owning workflow may use `spec-commit` after verification and with explicit commit authorization; protect mixed-file hunks and existing index entries under that helper's contract. Record the exact candidate SHA when committed, otherwise the base identity and run-owned diff/hash. On discard, restore only that recorded delta after checking it still matches. Never revert whichever commit happens to be HEAD. If later work overlaps, preserve it and report a recovery conflict. Reverting a committed candidate requires separate authorization for the exact Git mutation.

## Verify Safety Screen

Before first dry-run, screen Verify command for: rm -rf, fork bombs, curl|sh, embedded credentials, outbound writes. Block dangerous commands.

## Establish Baseline (Iteration 0)

For a working-system optimization that needs calibrated noise, multi-objective comparison or held-out confirmation, use the existing `spec-optimize` owner. This explicitly selected lightweight loop does not establish a second general development route or claim those guarantees.

Before mutation, check that the fixed measurement rejects a cheap relevant shortcut (such as empty/constant output or omitted required work) using available authorized inputs. A passing optional Guard does not establish task correctness. If the metric rewards a shortcut, repair measurement before beginning a separately identified run; do not optimize against the broken score.

1. Run Verify command → extract numeric metric
2. Record as iteration 0 in TSV: `0\t{timestamp}\t{commit}\t{metric}\t0.0\t{guard}\t-\tbaseline\tinitial state`
3. Exclusively create a unique output directory under `autoresearch/` using timestamp plus a random suffix; never reuse or truncate a same-minute run. Check for existing recoverable state before creating a new run.
4. Write TSV header: `# metric_direction: {direction}\niteration\ttimestamp\tcommit\tmetric\tdelta\tguard\tguard-metric\tstatus\tdescription`

## Iteration Loop

For each iteration (1 to max_iterations, or unbounded):

### Phase 1: Review (read git history as memory)
- Read last 10-20 lines of results TSV
- Run `git log --oneline -20` — see what worked/failed
- If last iteration was "keep", inspect its recorded base/candidate delta, which may remain uncommitted.
- Identify: what worked, what failed, what's untried

### Phase 2: Modify
- Based on review, make ONE focused change to improve the metric
- Change must be atomic — one logical unit of work

### Phase 3: Capture Candidate
- Record the candidate's source identity and recoverable delta under Candidate and Git Ownership.
- Do not stage or commit before verification.

### Phase 4: Verify
- Run Verify command → extract new metric value
- Calculate delta from previous iteration
- Metric improved (correct direction) → candidate for keep

### Phase 5: Guard (if configured)
- Run Guard command. If it fails, discard only the recorded candidate under Candidate and Git Ownership, regardless of metric improvement.

### Phase 6: Decide
- Check actual task behavior and the candidate diff before keep. An improved score from doing less required work or violating constraints is a discard even when Guard passes. Record the harness blind spot; do not patch the frozen metric within this run.
- **keep** — metric improved and guard passed; retain the candidate. An authorized commit is a separate owner-controlled checkpoint.
- **discard** — metric worsened; restore only the recorded run-owned delta.
- **crash** — verify/guard command failed; preserve logs, then apply the same scoped recovery.
- **no-op** — no change made this iteration
- **hook-blocked** — git hook blocked the commit
- **metric-error** — verify output is not a finite number; preserve the raw output and apply the same scoped recovery.

### Phase 7: Log
Append row to TSV: iteration, timestamp, commit/-, metric, delta, guard status, guard-metric, status, description

Persist and read back the raw command result, exact predicate, baseline/candidate byte identity and unique iteration ID alongside the row before selecting the next change. Resume reconciles existing identities and outputs before retrying unknown work; do not duplicate a measurement or invent a result from the summary. A failed write leaves the run incomplete.

### Eval Checkpoint
If --evals: check if current_iteration % interval == 0 → run checkpoint analysis.

### Bounded Check
If bounded: current_iteration >= max_iterations → exit loop, print summary.

## Summary (after loop ends)

Recheck original baseline against final candidate using the same frozen protocol before reporting confirmed improvement. Print total iterations, kept/discarded counts, starting and final metrics with units, and supported contributions. Do not add iteration percentages or convert ordinal score points into percentages; a zero baseline has no defined relative gain. Unknown noise, missing confirmation and absent holdout remain explicit limits. Keep shareable summaries free of secrets/private absolute paths; no automatic publication follows.

## Eval Checkpoint (--evals flag)

If --evals present:
- Compute interval: floor(max_iterations / 3), min 1. Fixed 10 if unbounded. Override: --evals-interval N.
- Every {interval} iterations, pause and analyze current results TSV.
- Print: `--- Eval Checkpoint (iterations {X}-{Y}) ---\nMetric: {start} → {end} ({delta}) | Kept: {n}/{total} | Trend: {up/flat/down}\n{one-line recommendation}\n---`
- If plateau 3+ checkpoints → recommend early stop.
- At loop end → full evals summary to evals-summary.md in output directory.

## Chain Handoff

After completion, write handoff.json to output directory: version "2.1.0", source "loop", timestamp, status (COMPLETE|USER_INTERRUPT|BOUNDED|ERROR), results_tsv path, findings[], config{goal, scope, metric, direction, verify}.
Invoke next target in --chain order. Propagate --evals flag.
